title: Everyday Science I
desc: Physics, chemistry, biology and IT basics

questions.q: The SI unit of force is:
questions.e: 1 newton is the force needed to accelerate 1 kg at 1 m/s². Joule is the unit of energy, watt of power and pascal of pressure.

questions.q: The SI unit of electric current is:
questions.e: Volt is potential difference, ohm is resistance (Ohm's law V = IR) and coulomb is charge.

questions.q: The speed of light in vacuum is approximately:
questions.e: Light takes about 8 minutes to travel from the Sun to the Earth.

questions.q: Sound travels fastest in:
questions.e: Sound needs a medium. It travels faster in solids than in liquids and gases because particles are closely packed.

questions.q: The chemical formula of water is:
questions.e: Water is formed by two hydrogen atoms and one oxygen atom. Pure water has pH 7.

questions.q: The pH of a neutral solution is:
questions.e: pH less than 7 is acidic and more than 7 is basic. Lemon juice is acidic; soap is basic.

questions.q: The most abundant gas in Earth's atmosphere is:
questions.e: Oxygen forms about 21%. Argon is about 0.93% and CO2 about 0.04%.

questions.q: The gas responsible for the greenhouse effect mainly emitted by burning fossil fuels is:
questions.e: Methane and nitrous oxide are also greenhouse gases. The ozone layer protects from UV radiation.

questions.q: Common salt is chemically:
questions.e: NaCl is used in food preservation and as a source for chlorine and caustic soda.

questions.q: Which metal is liquid at room temperature?
questions.e: Bromine is the only non-metal liquid at room temperature.

questions.q: The hardest natural substance is:
questions.e: Diamond and graphite are allotropes of carbon.

questions.q: The chemical symbol of gold is:
questions.e: Silver is Ag, iron is Fe, sodium is Na and potassium is K.

questions.q: The lightest element is:
questions.e: Hydrogen has atomic number 1. Helium is the second lightest.

questions.q: Which vitamin is produced in the skin by sunlight?
questions.e: Deficiency of Vitamin D causes rickets in children and osteomalacia in adults.

questions.q: Deficiency of Vitamin C causes:
questions.e: Vitamin A deficiency causes night blindness; B1 (thiamine) deficiency causes beriberi.

questions.q: Iron deficiency causes:
questions.e: Iodine deficiency causes goitre. Iron and iodine fortification are important child nutrition programmes.

questions.q: The powerhouse of the cell is:
questions.e: Mitochondria produce ATP. The nucleus contains DNA and controls cell activity.

questions.q: The human body has how many chromosomes?
questions.e: Down syndrome results from an extra chromosome 21. Sex chromosomes are XX for females and XY for males.

questions.q: The largest organ of the human body is:
questions.e: The liver is the largest internal organ. The skin protects against infection and regulates temperature.

questions.q: The normal human body temperature is:
questions.e: Fever is generally above 38°C. High fever in infants needs urgent medical attention.

questions.q: The normal adult heart rate is about:
questions.e: Newborns have a higher heart rate (100–160 bpm).

questions.q: Which blood group is the universal donor?
questions.e: AB positive is the universal recipient. Rh factor is named after Rhesus monkey.

questions.q: Which part of the blood helps in clotting?
questions.e: RBCs carry oxygen via haemoglobin. WBCs fight infection.

questions.q: Insulin is produced by the:
questions.e: Lack of insulin causes diabetes mellitus. World Diabetes Day is on 14 November.

questions.q: The 'master gland' of the human body is:
questions.e: It is located at the base of the brain and controls other endocrine glands.

questions.q: Dengue fever is transmitted by:
questions.e: Malaria is transmitted by female Anopheles mosquito. Cleaning stagnant water prevents mosquito breeding.

questions.q: Which disease is caused by a virus?
questions.e: Typhoid, TB and cholera are bacterial diseases. Polio is caused by poliovirus and prevented by vaccine.

questions.q: Tuberculosis is caused by:
questions.e: TB mainly affects lungs. DOTS treatment is used for TB.

questions.q: Malaria is caused by:
questions.e: Plasmodium is transmitted by the female Anopheles mosquito.

questions.q: Oral Rehydration Salts (ORS) are used to treat:
questions.e: Diarrhoea is a leading cause of child mortality. ORS and zinc are standard treatment.

questions.q: Photosynthesis occurs in the:
questions.e: Plants absorb CO2 and release oxygen in sunlight.

questions.q: Plants release oxygen during:
questions.e: Respiration releases carbon dioxide.

questions.q: The process of conversion of milk to curd is due to:
questions.e: It is an example of useful bacteria. Yeast is used for fermentation in bread.

questions.q: Which planet is known as the Red Planet?
questions.e: Venus is the hottest planet. Jupiter is the largest planet. Mercury is closest to the Sun.

questions.q: The largest planet in the solar system is:
questions.e: Jupiter has the Great Red Spot. Saturn has prominent rings.

questions.q: The Earth takes how long to complete one revolution around the Sun?
questions.e: Rotation takes 24 hours and causes day and night; revolution causes seasons.

questions.q: The nearest star to Earth is:
questions.e: Proxima Centauri is the nearest star after the Sun at about 4.2 light years.

questions.q: A lunar eclipse occurs when:
o: Moon comes between Sun and Earth
Earth comes between the Sun and the Moon
Earth is far from the Sun
questions.e: A solar eclipse occurs when the Moon is between the Sun and the Earth.

questions.q: Which part of the eye controls the amount of light entering?
questions.e: The retina has rods and cones. Myopia is corrected by concave lenses; hypermetropia by convex lenses.

questions.q: Which lens is used to correct short-sightedness (myopia)?
questions.e: Concave diverges light rays so the image falls on the retina.

questions.q: The device used to measure atmospheric pressure is:
questions.e: Hygrometer measures humidity; anemometer measures wind speed; seismograph measures earthquakes.

questions.q: Richter scale measures:
questions.e: Seismographs record earthquakes. The 2005 earthquake in Pakistan had magnitude 7.6.

questions.q: Which of the following is a renewable source of energy?
questions.e: Pakistan is working to increase solar, wind and hydropower share.

questions.q: Which fuel is used in CNG?
questions.e: Compressed natural gas is mainly methane.

questions.q: The full form of CPU is:
questions.e: The CPU is the brain of the computer and executes instructions.

questions.q: The full form of RAM is:
questions.e: RAM is volatile memory, its content disappears when power is off. ROM is non-volatile.

questions.q: 1 Byte equals:
questions.e: 1 KB = 1024 bytes; 1 MB = 1024 KB; 1 GB = 1024 MB.

questions.q: Which of the following is an input device?
questions.e: Output devices display results. A touchscreen is both input and output.

questions.q: HTTP stands for:
questions.e: HTTPS is the secure version. Websites use URLs.

questions.q: A computer virus is:
o: A malicious program that can replicate and damage files
questions.e: Antivirus software and safe browsing help protect devices. Children need online safety education.
